description: COPPER (Canadian Opportunities for Planning and Production of Electricity Resources) is a multi-period, optimisation-based capacity expansion model for the Canadian electricity system, developed by the SESIT group at the University of Victoria. The G-PST Open Tools Portal says it analyses the transition of Canada's electricity system under carbon management policies. The README (version 10.0) says it minimises total system costs, including investment and operation and maintenance, over an extended planning period, builds on the CREST framework of Dolter and Rivers (2018), and names Natural Resources Canada among the contributors. Coverage: Canadian provinces and their electricity systems; the regional resolution was not read. Format and access: Python source on GitLab (sesit/copper), with documentation on Read the Docs and a quick start that clones the repository and uses a conda environment; the repository showed activity on 25 September 2026. The model is also listed in the Canadian energy modelling hub inventory (cme-emh.ca). Licence: MIT (portal). Caveats: the documentation pages, input data sources and solver requirements were not read. Simulation uses: long-term generation and transmission expansion scenarios for Canada under emissions policies. Related records: SILVER (model-silver-variable-renewable-electricity-dispatch), from the same group, simulates dispatch for a chosen system, and IDEA (platform-idea-energy-transition-dashboard) visualises COPPER outputs.
